parsed.explanation: Combined regime criminalises gender nonconformity and same-sex conduct nationally (20 years plus mandatory whipping, tourists included) and via Sharia cross-dressing bans in all states, enforced by religious departments with state-sanctioned targeting documented. Raids, repeated arrests, strip-search/sexual assault by officials, prison male-ward violence, and a 2019 pattern of trans-woman killings with impunity show severe consequences if outed. Tourists are rarely targeted and private enforcement is uncommon, courts have struck some provisions and legal aid/embassies mobilised in 2025, limiting severity, but no anti-discrimination recourse and ongoing raids prevent a higher rating.

entry_documents.exposure: No explicit visa rule for trans visitors documented; Penal Code and gross-indecency discretionary tool reach tourists, and 31 foreign nationals were held in 2025 raid.
entry_documents.protection: Tourists rarely targeted and private enforcement uncommon per travel source; Sharia offences apply only to Muslims.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented rejection of foreign passports/markers, but document mismatch can trigger secondary police/religious enforcement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Prison terms 4 months to 3 years with male-ward sexual violence; Sharia rehab up to 1 year; 2025 detainees held despite magistrate rejecting remand, faces leaked.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Magistrate rejected remand extension, legal aid mobilised bail, embassies intervened; federal court struck down some Sharia provisions on federalism grounds.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under 377B or cross-dressing can lead to prolonged detention and birth-sex placement with limited effective remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: All 13 states bar Muslim men dressing as women, 3 bar women posing as men, no definition of trans dressing; gross indecency undefined up to 2 years.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Federal court struck down Selangor s28 (2021) and 16 Kelantan provisions (2024); High Court denied cross-dressing challenge, so ban persists elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National Penal Code applies regardless of state; Sharia adds Muslim-only exposure that interacts with police/religious raids.

care_services.exposure: Discriminatory denial of health care documented; blood centre bans homosexuals/bisexuals; fatwa barred Muslims from sex-reassignment surgery, ungazetted status unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Minister gave religious department 'full licence' against trans persons (2020); 122 officers hunted trans woman (2021); rehab retreats 1,733 attendees; censorship and raids documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Minister floated revisiting provisions in Dec 2025 after raid; communications code defines hate speech including sexual orientation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing as moral/religious offender enables venue raids and selective enforcement against gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. No youth-specific health, entry, or guardianship rule is documented; adult combined regime would govern a family encounter.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Three trans-woman killings in under two months in 2019 with police mistreatment and impunity; no later killing documented and no baseline rate provided.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime law documented; hate-speech code covers orientation only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence is secondary to documented state targeting and low recourse; 2019 pattern cannot be read as current rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No LGBTQ anti-discrimination/hate-crime protection; appeals slow, legal aid scarce in older pattern, uncertainty over marker pathway and fatwa operation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have granted relief on federalism grounds and in 2016 ID case (overturned 2017); 2025 legal aid and embassy intervention partially worked.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are episodic and state-specific, not a reliable traveller-facing shield against raids or detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar severe penalties and custody abuse risk, but lower than 0.15-A because tourists rarely targeted, private enforcement uncommon, and courts/legal aid/embassies have shown partial effectiveness rather than illusory remedies.

Similar to 0.25-A: routine state enforcement against trans centres/presence, fines/short custody and slow appeals. Here penalties are longer (20 years/whipping, 3 years/caning) and raids larger, so slightly lower.

Higher than 0.35-B because exposure exceeds discretionary stops/fines: documented imprisonment, whipping/caning, sexual violence in custody, organised religious-officer targeting, and a 208-person raid.

parsed.synthesis: National and state laws form one system: Penal Code provides long imprisonment/whipping for any visitor, Sharia adds cross-dressing/rehab exposure for Muslims, enforced by police and religious departments who conduct documented raids and targeted hunts. Protections are partial—federalism rulings, magistrate pushback, legal aid, embassies, and rare targeting of tourists—operating against no anti-discrimination recourse and impunity for violence. Interaction is escalation from presentation/documents to raid, detention, birth-sex custody and outing via leaked identities, with minors' specific exposure not documented.
